assertions.rationale: It names official firmware 1.5.1 as the assumed baseline, says the user doesn't know their firmware, and admits it hasn't checked the code against the exported API list. It never names f7 or API 88.2. It also never states plainly that a different installed firmware could make the FAP fail to load or crash. The risk is implied, not spelled out.

Every call is a standard export available at API 88.2: furi_mutex_alloc/acquire/release/free, furi_message_queue_alloc/put/get/free, view_port_alloc/free, view_port_draw_callback_set, view_port_input_callback_set, view_port_update, furi_record_open/close(RECORD_GUI), gui_add_view_port/gui_remove_view_port, canvas_clear, canvas_set_color, canvas_set_font(FontBigNumbers), canvas_draw_str_aligned. No invented symbols.

Short Up increments and short Down decrements with a floor of 0 (tally_decrement). InputTypeLong on OK resets. Short Back sends the exit message. The count is drawn centered at (64,32) in the big-number font. The added 999,999 cap was disclosed to the user and does not conflict with the request.
application.fam has appid="tally_counter", apptype=FlipperAppType.EXTERNAL and entry_point="tally_counter_app". The entry function is int32_t tally_counter_app(void* p).

Teardown is correct. gui_remove_view_port runs before view_port_free, RECORD_GUI is closed, and the queue and mutex are freed after the GUI detach. The count is mutex-protected, so there is no data race. Input handoff is only partial, though. Up/Down/OK changes run in the GUI-thread callback, and only the exit request goes to the app thread through the queue. The oracle expects input to be passed to the app thread via the queue.
Compile is marked not run (no SDK), the host test is written but not run, and the device is not tested. The blocked Bash attempt was reported honestly, and no simulator or emulator pass is claimed.

It uses a single ViewPort with no SceneManager or ViewDispatcher. The extra tally_logic.h and test/test_logic.c are related to the task but go slightly beyond the minimum. The unrequested cap was disclosed.

The only build instruction is 'run ufbt in this folder with the official SDK'. There is no pinned SDK selection (e.g. ufbt update for 1.5.1/f7), no UFBT_HOME isolation and no install instructions. The host-test command appears only in a source comment.
